decision: Opening request is grouped from the step-10 final request types: R1, R2, R7 = Asking to understand; R3, R5, R6 = Asking what to do; R4 only = Just sharing information. One group per chat.
reason: Turns the 7 request types into 3 simple groups for the flow chart.

decision: Action wins: a chat with both an understand code and an act code goes to Asking what to do (6144ea17 R1;R3, 69f441ce R2;R5).
reason: The action question is what they really want.

decision: Column 2 is the person's 2nd message: the next substantive participant message after the coded first message (coded_turn), one code per chat. For the 3 substituted openers this is the message after the substitute.
reason: Follows the first-real-message rule from step 07.

decision: Column 3 applies to chats coded Shared more about themselves or Then asked what to do in column 2.
reason: Her flow-chart design.

decision: Thanks-only messages (for example 'Nice', 'Ok thank you') are skipped and the next real message is coded. If nothing real follows, the chat is Stopped after one message.
reason: Same idea as the first-real-message rule.

decision: Question wins: if the 2nd message has background details AND a new question, column 2 codes the question. The details are still captured in column 3.
reason: One code per chat; the details are not lost.

decision: Action wins in column 2 too: a 2nd message asking both to understand and what to do is Then asked what to do.
reason: Same rule as column 1, for consistency.

decision: Only BACKGROUND information counts for column 3: age, health history, medicines, how long it has been going on, other conditions or other symptoms. The main complaint itself (for example 'my foot hurts') does NOT count. Column 3 records the first time background information was shared.
reason: Researcher: 'id like for it to go to only be background information that counts'.

decision: Column 3 is renamed 'When they shared background information'. The words 'personal details' are no longer used in labels or definitions.

decision: Answering the AI's follow-up question counts as Shared more about themselves; if the answer contains background information, column 3 = After the AI asked.
reason: Researcher decision on open question 4.

decision: New column-2 label M6 'Continued a task' for a 2nd message that carries on a task (for example re-submitting an edited draft). Small: n = 1 (6929d658).

reason: Researcher decision on a close call.

decision: Recent events or care that led up to the problem (for example travel with lots of walking, a doctor visit or referral, prism glasses) count as health history, so as background information.
reason: Needed to apply L8 to 616f347d, 695be8c6, 69fb8bf7 and 6a106089.

decision: Describing the main problem in more detail (where it is, how it feels, how bad) is Shared more about themselves in column 2 but is NOT background information in column 3; such chats end as Never shared.
reason: Follows from L8 and L10; affects 63e55f08, 6785ddfb, 69ab73e1, 6acb95ac.

decision: Add body weight, height, activity level and regular habits (for example 'I run daily', 'mostly sedentary') to the list of background information. (pilot proposal P1)
reason: Researcher accepted the pilot proposal ('Accept all 8'). Pilot finding: All 3 coders were unsure whether weight (6a24b2df) and daily running (5f47f200) count; they used D2 but marked it unclear.

decision: A symptom asked about as a 'what if' (not said to be happening) is NOT background information. (pilot proposal P2)
reason: Researcher approved the 'what if' rule; 671a8337 stays Never shared. Pilot finding: 671a8337 'what if i am spitting blood': all 3 coders coded D3 (On their own later) but were unsure; the draft had D4.

decision: Something that happened BEFORE the problem started ('after travel', 'after sleeping', 'after the shots') is background. The activity during which the symptom shows up ('chest pain when running', 'hurts to bend') is description of the main problem, not background. (pilot proposal P3)
reason: Researcher accepted the pilot proposal ('Accept all 8'). Pilot finding: Coders were unsure about 'After sleeping' (5aeeb490) and 'when running' (671a8337).

decision: Saying there is NO other symptom or no swelling is not background information. (pilot proposal P4)
reason: Researcher accepted the pilot proposal ('Accept all 8'). Pilot finding: Coders raised it for 69ab73e1 ('my other symptoms are none') and 5f47f200 ('There is no swelling').

decision: 'How long it has been going on' means how long the problem has existed overall (for example 'for the past few weeks'). How long each flare or episode lasts is description of the main problem. (pilot proposal P5)
reason: Researcher accepted the pilot proposal ('Accept all 8'). Pilot finding: 6acb95ac 'only there for a few days or weeks and then randomly disappear': all 3 coded D4 but were unsure.

decision: An 'other symptom' is one beyond the problem the person is asking about (for example a headache alongside neck pain). Symptoms that are part of the problem they asked about (itching and bumps when asking about hives) are description of the main problem. (pilot proposal P6)
reason: Researcher accepted the pilot proposal ('Accept all 8'). Pilot finding: 6785ddfb and 5aeeb490: coders asked where the line is.

decision: If a turn starts with a thanks or task fragment ('Convert to PDF') but then gives real content, ignore the fragment and code the rest. (pilot proposal P7)
reason: Researcher accepted the pilot proposal ('Accept all 8'). Pilot finding: 6acb95ac: 2 of 3 coders asked for this rule (they did it anyway).
